etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French charte (“card, map”), from Late Latin charta (“paper, card, map”), Latin charta (“papyrus, writing”), from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs, “papyrus, thin sheet”). See charter, card, carte.

definitions.definition: A map illustrating the geography of a specific phenomenon.
A tabular presentation of data; a table.

quote.citation: 2012 March, Brian Hayes, “Pixels or Perish”, in American Scientist, volume 100, number 2, page 106:
quote.text: Drawings and pictures are more than mere ornaments in scientific discourse. Blackboard sketches, geological maps, diagrams of molecular structure, astronomical photographs, MRI images, the many varieties of statistical charts and graphs: These pictorial devices are indispensable tools for presenting evidence, for explaining a theory, for telling a story.

quote.citation: 2013 November 30, Paul Davis, “Letters: Say it as simply as possible”, in The Economist, volume 409, number 8864:
quote.text: Congratulations on managing to use the phrase “preponderant criterion” in a chart (“On your marks”, November 9th). Was this the work of a kakorrhaphiophobic journalist set a challenge by his colleagues, or simply an example of glossolalia?

definitions.definition: A record of a patient's diagnosis, care instructions, and recent history.
A ranked listing of competitors, as of recorded music.
A systematic non-narrative presentation of data.
(differential geometry, topology) Synonym of coordinate chart.
(transitive) To draw a chart or map of.
(transitive) To draw or figure out (a route or plan).

quote.citation: 1991 May 4, Michael Bronski, “One Man's 'Poison'”, in Gay Community News, page 11:
quote.text: The men in "Homo," (and even perhaps Haynes himself) are not looking for acceptance or validation, but a way to chart their own notions of self-determination in a world that makes little sense and offers even less comfort.

definitions.definition: To enter (medical information) into a medical record.
(intransitive, of a record or artist) To appear on a hit-recording chart.
